title: Compound interest by repeated calculation
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The bank's compound interest point is a Year 12 formula approach (multiply by (1 + r) for each period), while the new point builds compound interest period by period and compares it with simple interest, so it is taught at a different depth for Year 11.

draft.title: Compound interest by repeated calculation
card: With compound interest, the interest is added to the balance at the end of each period. In the next period, interest is earned on the new, larger balance.
To work it out, find the interest for one period, add it to the balance, then repeat. Interest for a period = balance × rate for that period.
Example: $1000 at 10% per year for 2 years. Year 1: 10% of $1000 = $100, so the balance is $1100. Year 2: 10% of $1100 = $110, so the balance is $1210.
Simple interest on $1000 at 10% for 2 years is $200, so the balance would be $1200. Compound interest gave $210 because the year 1 interest earned interest.
draft.remember: Compound interest is added to the balance each period, so later interest is worked out on a bigger amount.

a.q: Ava invests $2000 at 5% per year, compounded yearly. What is the balance after 2 years?
a.why: Year 1: 5% of $2000 = $100, so the balance is $2100. Year 2: 5% of $2100 = $105, so the balance is $2205. $2200 is the simple interest answer, which works out interest on $2000 both years.
a.clue: Year 2 interest is worked out on the new balance.

b.q: Liam borrows $5000 at 10% per year, compounded yearly, and repays nothing for 3 years. How much more does he owe than with simple interest at the same rate?
b.why: Compound: $5000 becomes $5500, then $6050, then $6655, so the interest is $1655. Simple interest is 3 × $500 = $1500. The difference is $155. $1655 is only the compound interest, not the difference.
b.clue: Find both interest amounts, then subtract.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: $2000 at 5% for 2 years gives $2205, and $6655 − $6500 gives a difference of $155.
